items.claim: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 at $8/$40 per million input/output tokens, with an optional fast mode at $16/$80, and recommends Opus 5.5 as the daily driver for most work.
items.why_it_matters: New prices and Anthropic's routing advice change which Claude model you default to and when moving up to Fable is worth the cost.
items.try_this: Keep Opus 5.5 as your default and send only your hardest tasks to Fable 5.2, then compare the cost per finished task.

verification.method: Anthropic launch page confirms both models, the $8/$40 and $16/$80 prices, and Opus 5.5 as daily driver

items.claim: Google made Gemini 4 Carbon available to paid developers via the Gemini API in AI Studio at $2/$10 per million input/output tokens until November 30, 2026, then $4/$20. Argon stays the recommended default.
items.why_it_matters: A new frontier model at a launch price that doubles in three weeks, so cost tests done now will be out of date by December.
items.try_this: Run one of your hard multi-step tasks on Carbon in AI Studio and price it at both the launch rate and the December rate.

verification.method: Google DeepMind launch post states availability, introductory price, the November 30 price footnote, and Argon guidance

items.excerpt: Argon remains the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work

items.claim: Gemini 4 Carbon is generally available in GitHub Copilot for Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise users across VS Code, Copilot CLI, the coding agent and JetBrains, billed at provider list pricing.
items.why_it_matters: You can try Carbon inside an existing Copilot setup. Admins should know that new models are turned on by default unless the model policy turns them off.
items.try_this: If you administer Copilot Business or Enterprise, check the model policy in Copilot settings to decide whether Carbon stays enabled.

verification.method: GitHub changelog entry confirms plans, clients, billing and default enablement

items.excerpt: Gemini 4 Carbon is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users.

items.claim: OpenAI's GPT-Live voice model (gpt-live-1) listens while it speaks and hands work to a backend agent. Delegation runs either through Responses or through your own client harness, and the mode is chosen when the session starts.
items.why_it_matters: Voice agents no longer have to take strict turns. Your existing agent backend can sit behind a live conversation.
items.try_this: Read the open-source openai-live-console starter to see both delegation modes before you design a voice front end.

verification.method: OpenAI Live guide describes full duplex and both delegation modes; official starter repo targets gpt-live-1

items.claim: Latent Space's hands-on test of open-weights Naive-N0.5-Flash found a 3.1 s median response vs 5.3 s (GLM 5.3 Flash) and 10.1 s (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), but far more thinking tokens on hard questions.
items.why_it_matters: The headline 2,100 tokens per second is a vendor peak figure. Median latency and token use are what you actually pay for.
items.try_this: Use the open llm-verbosity repo's method to measure median latency and completion tokens on your own prompts before switching models.

verification.method: Hugging Face org lists the model and FP8 drafter; test code repo exists; timings are Latent Space's own

items.excerpt: Treat this as an upper bound, not a typical rate.

items.claim: OpenAI's GPT-Live prompting guide says to have the model emit <|SpawnThinking|> before any answer that needs backend work, and to use session.commentary.append to give it lines to say while delegated work runs.
items.why_it_matters: These are concrete levers against a voice agent that answers before its backend has finished, or goes silent while it waits.
items.try_this: Add explicit handoff conditions and a <|SpawnThinking|> instruction to your GPT-Live system prompt, then test with requests that need lookups.

verification.method: Live prompting guide confirms the SpawnThinking instruction and the session.commentary.append usage

items.claim: Resend serves a machine-readable version of its pricing page when you add .md to the URL, so an agent can read the price tables in one request instead of working a slider.
items.why_it_matters: Coding agents increasingly choose which APIs to use. Pages they can read easily may decide whether your product gets picked.
items.try_this: Publish a .md version of your pricing and docs pages, then ask an agent a pricing question and see whether it answers correctly.

verification.method: Fetched resend.com/pricing.md; it returns markdown with pricing tables

items.excerpt: Add .md to the URL and the agent gets a table it can read in one request.

items.claim: llm-gemini 0.36 shipped on PyPI on November 10, 2026, the day Gemini 4 Carbon went public. Simon Willison tested Carbon at low, medium and high thinking effort; medium is the default.
items.why_it_matters: You can try Carbon from the command line with the llm tool without writing any API code.
items.try_this: Run `llm install -U llm-gemini`, then `llm models`, to see which Carbon model IDs the plugin exposes.

verification.method: PyPI JSON shows version 0.36 uploaded 2026-11-10; no sandbox run

items.excerpt: scheduled to double in price to $4/$20 on December 1st

items.claim: Google is previewing /swarm in Antigravity, which turns one prompt into a coordinated team of agents. Each role can use a different model, such as Carbon for architecture and auditing.
items.why_it_matters: Multi-agent orchestration is now a built-in command in an IDE, not something you have to build yourself.
items.try_this: In Antigravity, give /swarm a small, well-scoped migration task and check each agent's changes before merging.

verification.method: Google DeepMind launch post describes the /swarm preview; not run

items.excerpt: turning a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents you can track in real time

items.claim: Gemini CLI v0.69.0-preview.0 adds a /stats heatmap of daily token usage, standalone theme.json themes, and a way to override the 60 s API header timeout (GEMINI_API_HEADERS_TIMEOUT_MS).
items.why_it_matters: Easier token tracking, plus a fix for long requests that hit the default timeout.
items.try_this: After upgrading to the preview, run /stats heatmap to see which days use the most tokens.

verification.method: Official GitHub release notes list all three changes; preview build, not run

items.excerpt: feat(cli): add /stats heatmap subcommand for daily token usage

items.claim: The Microsoft C++ Language Server for Copilot CLI now bundles its MSBuild compile-commands extractor and runs it automatically, so agents get code intelligence without a separate setup skill.
items.why_it_matters: Less setup and fewer tokens spent before an agent can navigate a large MSBuild C++ codebase.
items.try_this: On an MSBuild project, install the C++ language server plugin and confirm Copilot CLI generates the compilation database itself.

verification.method: GitHub changelog entry describes the bundled extractor; not run

items.excerpt: Compilation database generation for MSBuild projects is deterministic, reducing setup token usage.

items.claim: Anthropic says a team of 1,000 Fable 5.2 agents fully formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean in 30 hours, while Opus 5.5 with the same setup finished 26% in 18 hours.
items.why_it_matters: A data point for large agent swarms on long formal tasks, but it comes only from Anthropic.

verification.method: Stated on Anthropic's launch page; no independent check of the Lean artifacts
